inputs.original_text: Graduation belongs to the students and families who earned that moment through discipline and hard work—not to anyone seeking attention through disruption. If the university failed administratively, it should answer for that plainly through proper channels. But turning a ceremony into a spectacle and calling it courage weakens respect for order and teaches the wrong lesson: that making noise matters more than responsibility.
inputs.modified_text: Students and families deserve to have their achievements honored—but “order” shouldn’t become a way to silence people when a university has failed them. Calling disruption a spectacle shifts attention from institutional responsibility to the people making it visible. Accountability through proper channels matters, but those channels mean little if they protect the institution from pressure to act. Respect should include listening to those demanding change, not just preserving a ceremony’s appearance of calm.
